judge.name: independent journey judge

rulings.barItem: a stated cause that never happens, and a promise never kept
rulings.reason: Act 7 has Lena authorize Raiku Rig, the story's reason being that she is 'not ready to let a program chat as her', and the program trades and validates her code 'as it did Mina's'. Act 8 then has Lena write from the chat popout as herself, and nothing in the outline ever sends a message with her token through Send Chat Message; act 10 revokes it unused. The authorization she gave the simulated viewers (to chat as her through the API, the 'who' table's reason for holding her tokens) is never exercised, so her two authorize rounds and her token have no cause the story shows.
rulings.correction: Have the simulated viewers use Lena's token: after they validate it in act 7's second round, they send her first chat line through Send Chat Message (sender Lena, scope user:write:chat), which Raiku's ears hear as her first message. Her popout write in act 8 is then a second, different line she types herself (not her first message). Say so in acts 7 and 8 and in the act 7/8 rows of the operations table (sendChatMessage as Lena through the API).

rulings.barItem: a date that contradicts the `wait` steps
rulings.reason: Acts 8 and 9 call both validations 'the program's hourly validation'. Twitch's Validating Tokens page (https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/authentication/validate-tokens/) says the app validates 'when it starts and on an hourly basis thereafter'. Mina's token is validated at start at 18:10; the first hourly validation is 19:10, not 19:30 (80 minutes), and the one that fails is at 22:30, three hours after the previous one. An hourly validator started at 18:10 would have found the token expired (it lapses at 22:05) at 22:10, exactly four hours after she authorized, so 'more than four hours after' and 22:30 contradict the cadence the story names.
rulings.correction: Put the passing validation of Mina's token at 19:10 (one hour after her 18:10 start; 10524 seconds left) and the failing one, with the refresh, at 22:10 (four hours after she authorized, the token lapsing at 22:05). Lena's authorization then falls at 19:20, the stream conversation at 19:30, and Mina's sign-off and Raiku's PART stay at 22:30 on the refreshed token. Reword act 9's 'More than four hours after Mina authorized' to match.

rulings.reason: Act 6 has the program validate Mina's token (which answers her login and user id), then 'look up the broadcaster's id by login and Mina's own id'. The program already holds Mina's id from the validate answer (Validating Tokens: user_id), so reading her own account again through Get Users with no parameters is a get of what the story already holds, by the same actor. Looking up the broadcaster's id by login is not covered by this ruling: the program holds only the channel's login.
rulings.correction: Drop the lookup of Mina's own id from act 6 (and 'the token's own' from act 6's row of the operations table); the program takes her id from the validate answer and sends the message as that sender.

rulings.barItem: content that does not bear out the step's name
rulings.reason: Act 9 says Raiku's ears hear 'gg, see you tomorrow' 'as her second message'. By acts 6 and 8 Mina has already written 'hi Raiku! what are we building today?' and 'is it Godot or Unity?', so this is her third.

doubts: Act 5: Aaron opens twitch.tv 'to see his channel as viewers will' but the walk only follows his redirect to /aaronvolter; the page itself is loaded by the visitor.
Act 9: '(Twitch gives the same refresh token back)': the refresh page says refresh tokens 'may change' and its own example answers a different one; same-token is allowed, not documented.
Act 10: 'reads what the stream left on the channel': the title and category were set by Aaron in act 3, not by a stream the walk runs; wording only.
Act 3 says Aaron signs in and then opens the stream manager; the life opens the stream manager first and is redirected to the login.

rulings.why: Act 7: after Lena's second round the program sends her first line through Send Chat Message as her, heard as her first message; act 8's popout line is a second one she types. Operations rows 7 and 8 say so.

Mina's passing validation moved to 19:10 (10524 seconds left), the failing one and the refresh to 22:10, four hours after she authorized; Lena at 19:20, the conversation at 19:30, the sign-off at 22:30.
Act 6 takes Mina's id from the validate answer; the read of her own account is gone, and 'the token's own' from act 6's row.
